If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The test case and current bug report describe an infinite loop in the HelpFormatter's wrapping code that occurs when a word is too long to fit within the specified width. Examining the code, the printHelp method eventually calls printOptions, which calls renderOptions, which formats the options and descriptions and calls renderWrappedText to wrap text descriptions.

In renderWrappedText, the wrapping position is calculated using findWrapPos. If no wrap is possible (pos == -1), the text is appended as is (lines 808-815). Otherwise, the substring from 0 to pos is appended, followed by a newline, then the remainder of the text is padded with spaces (nextLineTabStop) and the loop continues.

The infinite loop occurs in the while loop starting at line 822. Inside the loop, it recalculates pos. If pos == -1, the text is appended and the method returns. However, if pos equals lastPos (the previous wrap point), this means the wrapping position has not moved — likely because no whitespace within width was found for the next segment. This condition throws a RuntimeException (line 836) to avoid an infinite loop.

The error implies that originally this RuntimeException was missing, resulting in the infinite loop mentioned. The test triggering the infinite loop is consistent with this scenario: a single word exceeding the width without whitespace causes findWrapPos to return the same position repeatedly, causing an infinite loop until OutOfMemoryError.

Hence, the infinite loop bug is caused by failing to detect or handle the case of no possible wrap in renderWrappedText's loop, when a single word is longer than the width. An explicit check and failure (exception) was added to avoid hanging infinitely.

No recent bugs about related text wrapping or infinite loop in HelpFormatter are visible, so this is likely a standalone fix in renderWrappedText.

Recommendation is to add a safeguard in HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText to detect no progress in wrap position and avoid infinite loop by throwing a RuntimeException. This matches line 836 code which includes a CLI-162 tag (matching bug report name), indicating this method is the bug location and must have been patched for this bug.

Therefore, the root cause lies in the lack of a break or error when wrapping very long words in HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText. The fix is the check on line 834-836.

Summary:
- HelpFormatter.printHelp calls renderWrappedText 
- renderWrappedText tries to wrap long strings by breaking at whitespace 
- When a very long word has no whitespace to wrap within width, findWrapPos returns the same position repeatedly 
- This causes an infinite loop in the while(true) loop as pos never advances 
- Fix is to detect pos == lastPos and throw exception to break loop and alert user 
- Test reproduces this by setting width=20 and a long word in option description triggering the bug

This detailed evidence from the code and test aligns perfectly with the bug report's problem description.

Suggested fix location: HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
